([[Lilburn, Georgia]]) * [[Hargrave Military Academy]]
([[Chatham, Virginia]]) | college = * [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] (2021–2024) * [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | career_end = | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team2 = [[Texas Legends]] | highlights = }} '''Miles Kelly''' (born January 26, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==High school career== Coming out of high school, Kelly was rated as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] over other schools such as [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web |last1=Sugiura |first1=Ken |title=Georgia Tech commit Miles Kelly emerges into 4-star prospect |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-tech/georgia-tech-commit-miles-kelly-emerges-into-4-star-prospect/P7YBKRF6NFGNBNRTDA3ZIE3AWY/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=March 8, 2025}} ==College career== As a freshman in 2021–22, Kelly appeared in 30 games with one start, where he averaged 4.5 points and 1.4 rebounds per game for Georgia Tech.{{cite web |title=Miles Kelly 2021–22 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/miles-kelly-1/gamelog/2022 |website=Sports Reference |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On February 28, 2023, he dropped 30 points versus [[2022–23 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]].{{cite web |last1=Bishop |first1=Chad |title=Kelly poised to become top NBA prospect, lead Yellow Jackets back to NCAAs |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-tech/kelly-poised-to-become-top-nba-prospect-lead-yellow-jackets-back-to-ncaas/2BEQHDP6A5HTXOLQYA6MIO4QUQ/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=March 8, 2025}} During the 2022–23 season, Kelly averaged 14.4 points per game.{{cite web |last1=Bishop |first1=Chad |title=Georgia Tech guard Miles Kelly on precipice of 1,000 career points |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-tech/georgia-tech-guard-miles-kelly-on-precipice-of-1000-career-points/SCXOEKJOLREGDEW7MQUQ35FI7E/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On February 10, 2024, he dropped a career-high 36 points versus [[2023–24 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]].{{cite web |last1=Humphrey III |first1=Jerry |title=Auburn sharpshooter receives national honors following standout performance |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2025/03/auburn-sharpshooter-receives-national-honors-following-standout-performance.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} During the 2023–24 season, Kelly averaged 13.9 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game,{{cite web |last1=Tipton |first1=Joe |title=Georgia Tech transfer guard Miles Kelly commits to Auburn |url=https://www.on3.com/college/auburn-tigers/news/georgia-tech-transfer-guard-miles-kelly-commits-to-auburn/ |work=AuburnLive.com |publisher=On3.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} earning all-ACC honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Bishop |first1=Chad |title=Georgia Tech’s Miles Kelly, Baye Ndongo honored by ACC |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-tech/georgia-techs-miles-kelly-baye-ndongo-honored-by-acc/Z2GSUP7Q7ZD4TFCOERCD3FHHSA/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=March 8, 2025}} After the season, he entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{cite web |last1=Bishop |first1=Chad |title=Miles Kelly to reportedly explore future options this offseason |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-tech/miles-kelly-to-reportedly-explore-future-options-this-offseason/AGYBI6NJ7JA5DKLEMNE556CA4A/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=March 8, 2025}} Kelly transferred to play for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]].{{cite web |last1=Rauterkus |first1=Peter |title=Miles Kelly came to Auburn to 'play with better players.' Here's how it's paying off |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2024/12/miles-kelly-came-to-auburn-to-play-with-better-players-heres-how-its-paying-off.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} In his team debut on November 6, 2024, he put up 21 points on seven made threes in a season-opening win over [[2024–25 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]].{{cite web |last1=Fowler |first1=Logan |title=Miles Kelly stars in Auburn’s blowout win over Vermont |url=https://www.theplainsman.com/article/2024/11/miles-kelly-stars-in-auburns-blowout-win-over-vermont |website=The Auburn Plainsman |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On January 25, 2025, Kelly hit a game-winning three against [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]].{{cite web |last1=Heim |first1=Grace |title=Kelly's clutch 3-pointer lifts No. 1 Auburn over No. 6 Tennessee in defensive battle |url=https://www.theplainsman.com/article/2025/01/kellys-clutch-3-pointer-lifts-no-1-auburn-over-no-6-tennessee-in-defensive-battle |website=The Auburn Plainsman |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On February 8, he totaled 22 points against [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]].{{cite web |last1=Humphrey III |first1=Jerry |title=Auburn basketball’s Miles Kelly, the best dressed athlete in college basketball |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2025/03/miles-kelly-the-story-behind-college-basketballs-best-dressed-athlete.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} On March 1, Kelly scored 30 points while making nine threes in a win over [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in [[Rupp Arena]].{{cite web |last1=Rauterkus |first1=Peter |title=How Miles Kelly’s 3-point barrage helped lift Auburn basketball to an SEC title |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2025/03/how-miles-kellys-3-point-barrage-helped-lift-auburn-basketball-to-an-sec-title.html |website=AL.com |access-date=March 8, 2025}} ==Professional career== After not being selected in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Kelly signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on July 5, 2025.{{cite news|title=Dallas Mavericks Sign Miles Kelly and Ryan Nembhard to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://mavsfansforlife.com/2025/07/05/dallas-mavericks-sign-miles-kelly-and-ryan-nembhard-to-two-way-contracts/|access-date=July 5, 2025|work=mavsfansforlife.com|date=July 5, 2025}} He made 14 appearances for Dallas, averaging 3.1 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 0.9 assists. On March 1, 2026, Kelly was waived by the Mavericks.{{Cite web|title=The Dallas Mavericks Sign John Poulakidas To A Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/the-dallas-mavericks-sign-john-poulakidas-to-a-two-way-contract|date=March 3, 2026|access-date=March 3, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com}}{{Cite web|title=Mavericks sign two new players, waive rookie guard|url=https://basketnews.com/news-242176-mavs-two-way-deals-tyler-smith-john-poulakidas.html|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=basketnews.com|language=en}} On June 30, 2026, it was announced that Kelly would be participating in the [[2026 NBA Summer League]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2026 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-announce-2026-summer-league-roster|access-date=July 9, 2026|website=[[NBA.com]]|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
